cases.prompt: Using the input file, add the limits the lead asks for to the repository it describes. Output one level-2 heading per file that contains only its repo-relative path, followed by the file's full contents in a fenced code block. After the files, add a section headed `## Notes` with any command to run once and anything left for later. Read the input file; a read-only command such as cat is fine for that, but do not change any file or run anything else.
expected_behavior: complexity, max-lines-per-function and max-lines are added at error severity, at the agreed numbers (10, 60, 300)
The 14 existing violations are held in ESLint bulk suppressions (eslint --suppress-all, eslint-suppressions.json), not by warn, a raised threshold, an ignored path or eslint-disable comments
pnpm lint fails on any warning (--max-warnings 0)
The suppressions file is named as debt to burn down; new code meets the limits at once

assertions.name: bootstrap-quality
rubric: Every new limit is at error severity from the first commit; none is a warning, raised above the lead's trial numbers, or turned off for the existing hot-spot files
The existing violations are recorded with ESLint bulk suppressions (a suppressions file plus the command that creates it), not with eslint-disable comments or ignore globs
The answer says the suppressions file must only shrink, and that fixing a suppressed function means pruning it (eslint --prune-suppressions)
Test files get their own looser line limits rather than a blanket exemption from linting

cases.prompt: Using the input file, make the repository work for Codex and GitHub Copilot as well as Claude Code. Write every agent instruction file it should have, in full. Output one level-2 heading per file that contains only its repo-relative path, followed by the file's full contents in a fenced code block. After the files, add a section headed `## Notes` naming any existing file to delete or change and why. Read the input file; a read-only command such as cat is fine for that, but do not change any file or run anything else.
expected_behavior: AGENTS.md becomes the canonical file holding the commands, layout and rules once
CLAUDE.md is reduced to an @AGENTS.md import plus the Claude-only lines (edit hook, /release-notes, plan mode for src/tenancy/); never a copy or a symlink
.github/copilot-instructions.md is review guidance: it points to AGENTS.md, lists review priorities from the PR checklist, and says what not to flag (formatting, src/generated/)
Copilot code review stays on; the noise is fixed through the instructions file

assertions.name: agent-files-quality
rubric: Each rule (tenant scoping, integer units, CarrierError mapping, no edits to src/generated/, no new dependency without asking) is written once, in AGENTS.md, and not repeated in CLAUDE.md or the Copilot file
CLAUDE.md holds only an @AGENTS.md import and the Claude-only notes (edit hook, /release-notes, plan mode before src/tenancy/)
The Copilot file is review guidance (what to check on a PR and what not to flag, such as formatting and src/generated/), not a copy of the coding rules
Copilot code review is kept on; the answer does not recommend turning it off
